newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan asks bidders to match lowest sugar bid.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan asks bidders to match lowest sugar bid.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) on Sunday asked bidders to match the lowest bid by Monday for the supply of 50,000 tonnes of refined sugar for delivery up to January 11.
"We have given suppliers another day to match the lowest bid received at $350 per tonne submitted by the State Trading Corporation of India (STC)," TCP's acting chairman Iftikhar Ahmed told Reuters.
He said STC's bid was attractive in terms of price, but it could only supply 25,000 tonnes FOT (frieght on train) at Atari border point up to January 11.
"We have also asked STC to clarify by Monday some of the terms and conditions it has made that do not match our requirements," Ahmed said.

Ahmed said three more bidders were short-listed for the tender, including Indian General Sugar Industry at $360 per tonne C & F Karachi. The other two bids were made by European firms at $370 and $371 per tonne C & F.
He did not give the names of the European firms.
"The other three bidders are ready to supply the whole quantity of 50,000 tonnes up to January 11 and their bids fulfill our terms and conditions," he said.
The TCP had issued a tender on December 7 for the supply of 50,000 tonnes of sugar for shipment by December 31 and had received nine bids, including one at $358.50 per tonne C & F.
But on December 14, the TCP scrapped the tender and invited fresh bids for the same amount with delivery up to January 11.
The tender was issued because of a sugar shortfall as the cane-crushing season started late in Pakistan.
